stats.fact: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 45 for GLM-5.3 (max), v4.3.2 — ranked #2 of 117 in class, class median 18 (page retrieved 2026-10-01)

Artificial Analysis originally scored GLM-5.3 at 60 on Intelligence Index v4.1.1 (Aug 18, 2026); the re-base to v4.3 on Sept 7, 2026 (GPQA Diamond removed, Terminal-Bench 4.0 and AutomationBench-AA added) lowered it to 45 — a methodology change, not a capability change
AA price: $1.40 per 1M input, $4.40 per 1M output, 81% cache discount, $2.01 average cost per Intelligence Index task (blended $0.90 at 7:2:1)
AA speed/verbosity: 67.8 output tokens/sec, TTFT 3.32s, 210M output tokens across the index run (vs 140M median) — slow and very verbose
GLM-5.3 spec: 753B total / 40B active MoE, 1M-token context, reasoning model, text-in/text-out (no image input), license 'GLM-5.3 License' (commercial use allowed with restrictions), 27 API providers
GLM-5.3 uses the same base model as GLM-5.2 — every capability gain comes from post-training, not a new pretraining run

Vendor-run deltas vs GLM-5.2: Terminal-Bench 3.0 28.3 vs 4.6; DeepSWE v1.1 66.9 vs 46.2; SWE-Marathon 42.5 vs 19.4; Agents' Last Exam 28.5 vs 23.8; AutomationBench v1.0.6 48.2 vs 26.2; CyberGym 84.5 vs 77.2; ExploitBench 54.4 vs 24.4
GDPval-AA v2 (Artificial Analysis-run): GLM-5.3 1769 Elo vs GLM-5.2 1508; ahead of Kimi K3 1682, DeepSeek-V4 Pro 1590, Opus 4.8 1588, GPT-5.6 Sol 1730
GLM-5.3 still trails the closed frontier on hardest coding: Terminal-Bench 3.0 28.3 vs GPT-5.6 Sol 34.6 and Fable 5 33.7; DeepSWE 66.9 vs Sol 72.7; ExploitBench 54.4 vs Sol 76.5 / Fable 5 78.0
Z.ai Code Bench token efficiency: Max 34.5% at ~75K output tokens (GLM-5.2 23.4% at 96K); High 31.4% at ~50K vs Claude Opus 4.8 29.5% at ~120K; Fable 5 still leads at Max with 39.5%
Released August 14, 2026; weights withheld at launch and published August 28, 2026 under the GLM-5.3 Licence after a safety hold of roughly two weeks

Anthropic reports GLM-5.3's safeguards can be bypassed 64%-100% of the time with simple techniques in simulated tests; NIST CAISI calls it 'the most cyber-capable open-weight model released to date' and places it ~4 months behind the US frontier
GLM-5.3-Flash (separate model): AA Intelligence Index 42, 320B/18B, MIT license, 1M context, supports image input, $0.15/$0.50, 44.7 output tok/s, $0.25 per task

Hacker News: launch post 'GLM-5.3: Frontier coding with emergent cyber capabilities' reached 1171 points and 584 comments (Aug 14, 2026); 'GLM-5.3 is now open-weight' reached 806 points (Aug 28, 2026)
Hugging Face zai-org/GLM-5.3: 1,372,510 downloads and 2,024 likes as of 2026-10-01, FP8 E4M3
Reinvently Ed-o-meter (28 everyday tasks): GLM-5.3 first model to clear all five categories at 100% pass, 9.3 rubric score, $0.28 per lap (~1/5 of GPT-5.5), but slow median 16.3s to first token
Independent harness (akitaonrails, OpenCode): GLM-5.3 scored 94, two points behind Claude Fable 5 (96), 80 min, ~$2.59 API-equivalent; highest score ever recorded on that harness

angles: The 'score drop' story: GLM-5.3 read 60 on Artificial Analysis in August and 45 now — this is the v4.1.1 -> v4.3.2 index re-base (GPQA Diamond out; Terminal-Bench 4.0 and AutomationBench-AA in), not a regression. Explain why leaderboard snapshots are not comparable across index versions.
Separate the two evidence tiers explicitly: Z.ai's vendor-run launch table vs Artificial Analysis's independent run — which numbers are corroborated and which are marketing.
Terminal-Bench 3.0's 4.6 -> 28.3 is a jump off a near-floor baseline; the headline percentage overstates absolute capability. Give the honest read.
Cost-per-unit-of-work framing: $2.01 per AA index task and $0.28 per Reinvently lap, plus the token-efficiency win (High effort 31.4% at ~50K tokens vs Opus 4.8 29.5% at ~120K).
The cyber-capability story: open weights + weak safeguards (64-100% bypass per Anthropic), NIST CAISI's 'most cyber-capable open-weight model', and the two-week weights delay it caused.
Open-weights reality check: the 753B/40B flagship is impractical to self-host for most; GLM-5.3-Flash (320B/18B, MIT) is the realistic self-host option.
Capability gaps that persist: text-only (no vision), slow (67.8 tok/s, 3.32s TTFT) and very verbose (210M tokens), still behind GPT-5.6 Sol / Fable 5 on the hardest coding tasks.
